name: Svalbard, Norway
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 11.3 m across on an Arctic island, 78 degrees north. It hears S-band and X-band radios.
why_it_matters: It is so close to the North Pole that a spacecraft in a polar orbit flies past on most orbits. A spacecraft in a low-tilt orbit never comes into view.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide. The price is NASA's 2018 planning rate per pass of up to 30 minutes.

name: Fairbanks, Alaska
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 11.3 m across in Alaska, 65 degrees north. It hears S-band and X-band radios.
why_it_matters: It is far north, so it sees a polar-orbiting spacecraft several times a day. It sees fewer passes than a station nearer the pole.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide. The guide's detail table for AS1 (Table 7-3) gives a higher X-band G/T, 37.2 dB/K; the lower overview value is used.

name: Wallops Island, Virginia
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 11.3 m across on the east coast of the United States, 38 degrees north. It hears S-band and X-band radios.
why_it_matters: A middle-latitude station can see spacecraft in lower-tilt orbits such as the space station's, which polar stations cannot. It sees only a few passes a day.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide. The guide's detail table for WG1 gives a lower S-band G/T, 22.8 dB/K at 41 degrees elevation.

name: McMurdo, Antarctica
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 10 m across in Antarctica, 78 degrees south. It hears S-band and X-band radios.
why_it_matters: It is as close to the South Pole as Svalbard is to the North Pole. Using both gives a polar-orbiting spacecraft a contact near each end of most orbits.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide.

name: Singapore
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 9.1 m across almost on the equator. It hears S-band and X-band radios.
why_it_matters: A station on the equator can see a spacecraft in any orbit. It sees each one only two or three times a day.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide. The guide's detail table for SI1 gives a higher X-band G/T, 35.4 dB/K; the lower overview value is used.

name: Santiago, Chile
price_source: SCaN Mission Operations and Communications Services (MOCS), SCaN-MOCS-0001 Revision 1, Table 5-2, https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/simplex/pdf_files/SCaN-MOCS-0001_Rev-1.pdf
description: A dish 9 m across in South America, 33 degrees south. It hears S-band radios only.
why_it_matters: A station is only useful if it listens on your radio's frequency. This one cannot hear an X-band transmitter.
source: Near Earth Network (NEN) Users' Guide, 453-NENUG Revision 4, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Table 2-1, https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/2021APMIDEX/pdf_files/453-UG-002905.pdf
notes: Figures are from Table 2-1 of the guide.
